grounding.derivation: src-verify-doc describes verification by heartbeats to voters; src-verify-contract identifies confirmation of leadership as its purpose, including prevention of stale reads. src-config-types distinguishes Voter and Nonvoter roles. The actual threshold is quorumSize, whose src-lease definition counts voters only. Therefore the support count being compared against that threshold must count eligible voters: an arbitrary nonvoter cannot substitute for one of those participants. The code that registers all replication peers and counts notifyAll results is the subject of comparison, not normative authority that weakens this requirement. The requirement is necessary eligibility accounting, not an assertion that a quorum always succeeds or that every excess tally causes an observed stale read.
grounding.applicability: Stable mixed-suffrage configuration, locally active leader verification, response identity known independently of its success value.
alternatives: Independent voter-only lease checking can later demote a leader, but does not change the participant eligibility of this verification tally.

feedback.answered: A1: each leader creates a commitment object containing current voters and a startIndex equal to the first log index of its term. Local StoreLogs success and follower replication success provide match support; recalculate requires a majority prefix at or above startIndex before notifying the leader. A2: candidate campaigns use a fresh response channel per electSelf call, send one request per configured voter, persist the self vote and count granted responses; requestVote checks term, candidate eligibility, prior persisted vote and log freshness. A leader creates fresh replication/commitment state and a no-op; on leaving leadership it closes replication stop channels, fails inflight/verification futures and clears leader state. These mechanisms connect authority tenure to eligible support rather than carrying the previous commitment object into a new term. Configuration changes are admitted only after the latest configuration and an entry in the current term are committed. Follower appendEntries rejects old terms, validates the preceding term, truncates conflicting supplied entries, stores replacements, and then advances commitment to min(LeaderCommitIndex, local last index). The producer independently captures LeaderCommitIndex and limits supplied entries to MaxAppendEntries. processLogs queues local command entries through fsmMutateCh; FSM.Apply has an interface promise that entries are committed by a majority. This identifies a question about a bounded matching request followed by a divergent local suffix, not yet an executed violation.

formation.explanation: A1: leader dispatch assigns term/index and persists logs before recording its match and notifying peer replicators. Per-peer requests carry previous prefix, bounded entries and commit index; success supplies stored-prefix support to a captured commitment object. Only configured voters count, and its majority index must reach the first entry of this leader term. The main loop consumes commit notification, marks configuration committed and queues logs. Followers validate term/previous prefix, truncate supplied conflicts and propagate leader commit accounting into their own queue. FSM execution and future completion occur later on the FSM goroutine. Snapshot transfer substitutes a persisted/restored prefix when logs are unavailable.

context.explanation: A2: contact timeout triggers a eligible local voter campaign; pre-vote probes where supported, then electSelf persists a new term/self vote and asks configured voters through a campaign-local response channel. Vote receivers reject ineligible/stale or less-up-to-date candidates and preserve one vote per term. Majority grants install leader state. Higher-term requests, replication higher-term responses, loss of lease quorum and committed removal can end tenure. Transfer first catches up its target then requests an accelerated campaign. Startup restores term, snapshot and membership history but starts as follower.

connection.explanation: Each tenure creates fresh commitment/replication objects, captures its term and sends a no-op; the current-term threshold constrains commitment of inherited history. Old RPC replies retain old campaign channels or commitment pointers, while follower term checks reject obsolete requests. Leader exit signals replication to stop and fails pending client/verify futures; it does not erase stored or already queued history. New authority is constrained by log freshness and recovered configuration. Configuration changes serialize after a current-term commit, then alter voter eligibility while retaining matching support for retained voters. Committed entries are separately consumed by the FSM, and a failed client future does not imply absence from later history. VerifyLeader is another authority consumer whose voter threshold and all-peer notifications have an unresolved eligibility relationship.

materials.text:
### Leader Write

Most write operations must be performed on the leader.

* RequestConfigChange - update the raft peer list configuration
* Apply - apply a log entry to the log on a majority of peers, and the FSM. See [raft apply](apply.md) for more details.
* Barrier - a special Apply that does not modify the FSM, used to wait for previous logs to be applied
* LeadershipTransfer - stop accepting client requests, and tell a different peer to start a leadership election
* Restore (Snapshot) - overwrite the cluster state with the contents of the snapshot (excluding cluster configuration)
* VerifyLeader - send a heartbeat to all voters to confirm the peer is still the leader

scope.description: Participant eligibility in the per-request VerifyLeader quorum tally, with an unchanged mixed voter/nonvoter configuration and no concurrent leadership/configuration transition during the measured accounting step.
assumptions: Correct peer identities and suffrage; non-Byzantine, well-formed acknowledgments.
An active verification request with initial self support and a configured voter-majority threshold.
excluded: Whether another leader is actually elected.

feedback.answered: A1: each leader creates a commitment object containing current voters and a startIndex equal to the first log index of its term. Local StoreLogs success and follower replication success provide match support; recalculate requires a majority prefix at or above startIndex before notifying the leader. A2: candidate campaigns use a fresh response channel per electSelf call, send one request per configured voter, persist the self vote and count granted responses; requestVote checks term, candidate eligibility, prior persisted vote and log freshness. A leader creates fresh replication/commitment state and a no-op; on leaving leadership it closes replication stop channels, fails inflight/verification futures and clears leader state. These mechanisms connect authority tenure to eligible support rather than carrying the previous commitment object into a new term. Configuration changes are admitted only after the latest configuration and an entry in the current term are committed. Follower appendEntries rejects old terms, validates the preceding term, truncates conflicting supplied entries, stores replacements, and then advances commitment to min(LeaderCommitIndex, local last index). The producer independently captures LeaderCommitIndex and limits supplied entries to MaxAppendEntries. processLogs queues local command entries through fsmMutateCh; FSM.Apply has an interface promise that entries are committed by a majority. This identifies a question about a bounded matching request followed by a divergent local suffix, not yet an executed violation.

formation.explanation: A1: leader dispatch assigns term/index and persists logs before recording its match and notifying peer replicators. Per-peer requests carry previous prefix, bounded entries and commit index; success supplies stored-prefix support to a captured commitment object. Only configured voters count, and its majority index must reach the first entry of this leader term. The main loop consumes commit notification, marks configuration committed and queues logs. Followers validate term/previous prefix, truncate supplied conflicts and propagate leader commit accounting into their own queue. FSM execution and future completion occur later on the FSM goroutine. Snapshot transfer substitutes a persisted/restored prefix when logs are unavailable.

context.explanation: A2: contact timeout triggers a eligible local voter campaign; pre-vote probes where supported, then electSelf persists a new term/self vote and asks configured voters through a campaign-local response channel. Vote receivers reject ineligible/stale or less-up-to-date candidates and preserve one vote per term. Majority grants install leader state. Higher-term requests, replication higher-term responses, loss of lease quorum and committed removal can end tenure. Transfer first catches up its target then requests an accelerated campaign. Startup restores term, snapshot and membership history but starts as follower.

connection.explanation: Each tenure creates fresh commitment/replication objects, captures its term and sends a no-op; the current-term threshold constrains commitment of inherited history. Old RPC replies retain old campaign channels or commitment pointers, while follower term checks reject obsolete requests. Leader exit signals replication to stop and fails pending client/verify futures; it does not erase stored or already queued history. New authority is constrained by log freshness and recovered configuration. Configuration changes serialize after a current-term commit, then alter voter eligibility while retaining matching support for retained voters. Committed entries are separately consumed by the FSM, and a failed client future does not imply absence from later history. VerifyLeader is another authority consumer whose voter threshold and all-peer notifications have an unresolved eligibility relationship.
